name: Route One 4-4-2

slots.why: Kicks long to the target man, so kicking and throwing matter.
Support full-back provides width for the early crosses.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Winger (Support) crosses early for the target man and second striker.
Defensive central midfielder wins the ball and passes it forward simply.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the second ball from the knock-downs.
Winger (Support) crosses early from the right.
Target man wins the long balls in the air and holds it up or flicks it on.
Advanced Forward runs onto the flick-ons. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A deliberately direct system that moves the ball forward early toward a physical target and runners attacking second balls.
whyGood: The Target Man gives long passes a destination while the AF, wide players and midfield compete for territory and knockdowns.
whyThisShape: A direct 4-4-2 that skips the midfield: long balls to a target man, with a second striker running onto flick-ons, and wingers crossing early. It is the least subtle system in the catalogue, and works when the forwards are physically stronger than the defenders.
whenToUse: When you have a big target man and a quick second striker, but weak technical midfielders; or against teams with small defenders.
whenNotToUse: Against tall, strong centre-backs who win the aerial duels, or when your squad is technical and would waste its passing.

instructionRationale.Much More Direct Passing: Long balls go straight to the target man, which is the point of the system.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Gets the ball forward before the defence has set.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: The second striker runs onto the flick-ons behind the defence.
instructionRationale.Hit Early Crosses: The wingers cross early for the target man, instead of dribbling.
instructionRationale.Counter: Attacks quickly when the ball is won.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Drops back into shape after losing the ball.
